newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amplats shares jump on mine, merger news.
newsitem.headline: Amplats shares jump on mine, merger news.

text.p: News that Anglo American Platinum Corp of South Africa plans to merge its platinum companies and a big new platinum mine sent its companies' shares to a day's high on Tuesday, dealers said.

Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd (Rusplat) climbed 100 cents to 72 rand with 121,500 shares changing hands and Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd rose 150 cents to 26.50 rand with 114,100 shares changing hands.
Amplats itself added 60 cents to 29 rand in a volume of 221,100 shares on an otherwise fairly quiet day.

Dealers said the Amplats' shares were strengthening on the announcment of the a new mine at Boschkoppie, in the Rustenburg area, and expansion of PP Rust's concentrator, which Amplats said would enhance its position as world leader in platinum.
"A new mine like that means that Amplats has got confidence in the future and that's likely to push the shares up for a whileing costs is also a positive thing," one dealer said.
Annual platinum output from Boschkoppie was expected to be about 250,000 ounces of refined platinum metal when full production is reached in 2002, the company said in a statement.
Amplats said the new projects would increase operational flexibility and cut costs.
But shares in smaller Lebowa PLatinum Mines Ltd shed eight cents to a day's low of 2.86 rand after gaining 20 cents to 294 cents on Monday.

Dealers were puzzled as to why Lebowa should slip, but added it could be due to speculation over the possible merger ratios which had yet to be announced and which the market seemed to fear would not favour Lebowa.
Amplats said on Tuesday it planned to merge its four listed companies which at present constitute the group -- Rusplat, Lebowa, PP Rust and Amplats itself.

"The concept of the merger, or bundling, has been in the market for a long time now. They still have to announce the terms of the deal and until then the market will determine the level the shares should be at," one dealer said.
Amplats said in a statement that it hoped to make a further announcement within two months detailing the proposed merger.
